title: The 3-restricted Edge-Connectivity of Strong Product Graphs
summary: An edge subset \( S \subseteq E(G) \) is called a 3-restricted edge-cut if $G-S$ is disconnected and each component of \( G - S \) contains at least three vertices. The 3-restricted edge-connectivity of a graph \( G \), denoted by \( λ_3(G) \), is defined as the minimum cardinality among all 3-restricted edge-cuts if there are at least one; otherwise, \( λ_3(G) = +\infty \). It is proved that $λ_3(G)\leqξ_3(G)$ if $G$ has a 3-restricted edge-cut, where $ξ_3(G) = \min \{ |[X, V(G) \setminus X]_G||X \subseteq V(G),|X| = 3 \text{ and } G[X] \text{ is connected}\}.$ If \( λ_3(G) = ξ_3(G) \),…
